3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to Noabad Taluq belonged to Maimuna Khatun. For arrear of revenue the suit land was sold in auction and one Md. Ishaque purchased the same on 06.04.1935 and got possession. Subsequently, the auction purchaser sold the suit land to the plaintiffs' predecessor Mvi. Abdur Rashid Chowdhury by a registered kabala dated 08.04.1943. That  Mvi. Abdur Rashid Chowdhury at his older age had been suffering, from rheumatic fever and taking advantage of his ailment the defendants surreptitiously got their names recorded in S. A. Khatian of the suit land. That at the death of Abdur Rashid the plaintiffs have inherited the suit land and have been possessing the same. But the defendants have been threatening the plaintiffs with dispossession and thus the plaintiffs have been compelled to file the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos.1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement. Their case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Maimuna Khatun. That Maimuna Khatun settled the suit land to one Krishna Kanta Chakravorty who got possession of the same. That as Krishna Kanta Chakravorty defaulted in payment of rent a rent suit was filed against him which was decreed and on the basis of that decree Rent Execution Case No.340 of 1932 was started and Mallika Bala Dey and Tulshi Bala Dey purchased the suit land in that rent execution case in the benami of their  trusted person Tofar Ali in the year 1932 and got possession and since then they had been possessing the same on payment of rent etc. Subsequently, Tofar Ali executed and registered a "muktinama" in favour of Mallika Bala Dey and Tulshi Bala Dey admitting them as real purchasers. On 07.04.1956 Mallika Bala Dey sold out her share to the defendant' No. 1 by registered kabala. Bala Dey died leaving defendant No.2 as her sole heir. Thus the defendant Nos.1 and 2 have become the owners of the suit land and they have also been possessing the same. The P.S. and B.S. khatians of the suit land have been recorded in the name of defendant Nos.1 and 2 and they have been paying rent of the suit land regularly. That the plaintiffs have got no right, title and possession in the suit land and as such the suit is liable; to he dismissed  with costs. 

 6. Mr. Abdul Momen Chowdhury, the teamed Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner, has mainly argued that the High Court Division has misconstrued and misinterpreted the exhibited documents and on erroneous and arbitrary finding that the sale certificate and writ or delivery of possession do not contain plot or khatian numbers arrived at a wrong decision; that in the sale certificate and in writ of delivery of possession, the 'Mahal" number and other required materials have been mentioned which sufficiently indicate that this suit land was sold in that auction and the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession are in respect of the suit land. The learned Advocate has submitted that the High Court Division over looked also the fact that the khatian of the suit land was duly mutated in the name of auction purchaser which fact also tells in favour of plaintiffs case. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner has argued also that the trial court, on meticulous examination and consideration of evidence came before it rightly found that the plaintiff proved his case by producing sufficient evidence both oral and documentary and has rightly decreed the suit; that the High Court Division did not at all consider the findings of the trial court and as such failed to come to a correct decision; that the High Court Division should have restored the judgment of the trial court and set aside the judgment of the appellate court. 

 11. It appears that both the parties adduced necessary documents to substantiate their respective case. The trial court though relying on the documents of the plaintiffs decreed the suit but the appellate court on meticulous examination of the documents produced by the contesting defendants found out that the admitted owner Maimuna Khatun settled the suit land in favour of Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by registered pasta dated 30.05.1927 and that the genuineness of this registered patta was proved from the relevant papers relating to Rent Suit No.1201 of 1931 and Rent Execution Case No.340 of 1932 the exhibited-D and J. The said documentary evidence proved it sufficiently that Maimuna Khatun filed that rent suit against Krishna Kanta Chakravorty for arrears of rent. The appellate court, therefore, rightly found that the registered patta dated 30.05.1927 showing settlement of the suit land in favour of Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by Maimuna Khatun was genuine one. This fact of settlement of the suit land to Krishna Kanta Chakravorty by Maimuna Khatun in the year 1927 makes out the plaintiffs case that one Md. lshaque purchased the suit land in auction in the year 1935 not true. It appears that the appellate court, on careful examination of the documents filed by the plaintiff, detected rightly that in the year 1935 the taluki right of Maimuna Khatun was sold in auction for arrears of rent and Md. Ishaque purchased the taluki right only of Maimuna Khatun in that auction. The appellate court also made Clear observation to the effect that at the time of purchase of taluki right by Md. Ishaque in the year 1935 Mallika Bala Dry and Tulshi Bala Dey were in possession of the suit land as tenants and that the plaintiff could not adduce any iota of evidence before the court to prove that the auction purchaser Md. Ishaque ejected those tenants from the suit land. The appellate court found out also that in the registered sale deed of the year 1956 executed by Mallika Bala Dey in favour of the defendant No.1 Mvi. Abdur Rashid (the purchaser from the auction purchaser Md. Ishaque) was men Boned as owner of the taluk. This fact also indicates sufficiently that Md. Ishaque purchased the taluki right only of Maimuna Khatun in auction held in the year 1935 and subsequently he sold that taluki right to Mvi. Abdul Rashid in the year 1943 and that Mallika gala Dey and Tulshi Bala Dey were the tenants under Md. Ishaque and thereafter under Mvi. Abdur Rashid. Admittedly, the P.S. khatian of the suit land has been recorded in the names of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 who acquired the suit land from Mallika Bala Day and Tulshi Bala Dey.
